title: Washington College appoints founding dean for Warehime School of Business
text:
Washington College appoints founding dean for Warehime School of Business
Caddie Putnam Rankin has been named the founding dean of the Warehime School of Business at Washington College, according to an Aug. 5 announcement. The school will welcome its first class of students later this month with the arrival of the Class of 2030.
Putnam Rankin, who is currently an associate professor of business management, has helped lead the process to design the school's mission, composition, and curriculum over the past two years. Washington College President Bryan Matthews said, “Over the past several years, Caddie has led the evolution of the Warehime School of Business. She shaped the school’s academic vision and developed an innovative curriculum that prepares students to lead in a rapidly changing global economy while remaining grounded in the enduring values of a liberal arts education. Having helped envision the Warehime School of Business from its earliest stages, Caddie is uniquely qualified to serve as its inaugural dean.”
Previously, Putnam Rankin served as associate dean for business and chair of business management. Her research focuses on corporate social responsibility, organizational legitimacy, professionalization, and how business can be a force for positive social impact. She earned her Ph.D. in Organizational Sociology from Emory University in 2011 and teaches courses including corporate social responsibility, strategic management, and nonprofit management.
The Warehime School was established through a $15 million gift from alumna Beth Warehime Rizakos. It aims to become a regional center for business innovation and provide graduates with opportunities to become ethical leaders prepared for global challenges.
Putnam Rankin said, "The extraordinary generosity of Beth Warehime and her family has made it possible for Washington College to build a new model for business education. The Warehime School of Business will prepare students not only to succeed in today’s economy but to shape tomorrow’s. By activating the liberal arts through interdisciplinary learning, global experiences, and hands-on engagement with industry and communities, we are empowering graduates to become innovative thinkers, principled decision-makers, and catalysts for meaningful change."
The school includes departments covering business management; economics; world languages and cultures; as well as international studies—offering students connections between business disciplines and fields such as policy or technology.
